backbone: Build blown-up Kähler products with two-prime integral torsion; a Hamiltonian involution realizes few fixed points, while torsion plus Smale handle cancellation computes the larger stable Morse number.
quote: For every integer m ≥ 1, we construct a simply connected closed Kähler manifold with stable Morse number $`80+1968m`$ and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly $`80+1952m`$ fixed points

backbone: Split by whether a zero-curvature plane exists: positive case by the companion classification; otherwise coupled integral Weyl-block inequalities plus equality analysis force a parallel splitting into two round spheres.
quote: The proof extends coupled estimates for the two Weyl curvature blocks to the boundary of the sectional-curvature cone and determines their equality case.

backbone: Induction on dimension; a least-area counterexample exists by compactness, has index above m+3, so a deformed Lorentz-distance sweepout plus min-max yields a smaller counterexample, a contradiction.
quote: A counterexample must therefore have a further negative direction for area.

backbone: Bound mean doubling growth via a multiscale subdivision tree: subtract affine profile parts, control stopped descents and persistent excursions by compactness-contradiction and packing, then transfer growth to nodal length.
quote: The contradiction argument below extracts a nonconstant profile, finds a nearby square with small affine excess relative to a nonzero slope, and transfers that square to Proposition~\ref{prop:stability}.

backbone: Assume bounded scalar curvature with a singularity; bubble-tree scale selection plus a static Einstein–Hilbert tree inequality force root Ricci energy to vanish, contradicting the prescribed change of the outermost scale.
quote: Functional change and the contradiction

backbone: Reduce U(10)-invariant Calabi flow to a scalar PDE; build a self-similar shrinking profile by certified shooting, then correct it to an exact compact solution via an ancient inverse and contraction.
quote: We construct a smooth Kähler metric in the Fubini–Study class of $`\mathbb{CP}^{10}`$ whose Calabi flow develops unbounded scalar curvature in finite time.

backbone: Reduce rigidity to uniform section balance (Trudinger–Wang); failure yields affine limit models with several directions, excluded by a coercive integral inequality valid through dimension nine, contradiction.
quote: Suppose that no uniform constant exists. Choose $k$-models and positive fibers for which the inclusion with constant $j$ fails.

backbone: Two-volume reduction plus classical structure of flat isoperimetric boundaries; nonstandard genus/vertex-pattern cases are excluded one by one via reflection symmetry, slicing and rationally certified scalar inequalities.
quote: Either \(\Sigma\) is a union of parallel planar surfaces, or \(\Sigma\) is connected. In the connected case:

backbone: Prove a localized Łojasiewicz-type gradient inequality for Gaussian area near the shrinker via a finite-jet obstruction, then propagate it with a bootstrap to finite length and unique convergence.
quote: Gradient inequalities connect small stationary defect to finite length of the rescaled flow.

backbone: Forward: Alexandrov comparison gives the distributional tensor bound via transport. Reverse chain: tensor bound to index inequality to Hessian comparison along geodesics to triangle comparison.
quote: From Hessian bounds to triangle comparison

backbone: Harmonic coordinates at every center and scale; heat averages and summable directional pinching control cumulative Gram matrices; a renormalization iteration with metric bootstrap yields an open bi-Lipschitz chart.
quote: Suppose inductively that \[ |P-u(x_j)|_{R(\rho_j,x_j)^{-1}}<c\rho_j, \qquad \rho_j=4^{-j}\rho_0. \]

backbone: Glue two product pieces by a shear; flat-torus theorem shows no CAT(0) action (contradiction); explicitly build a concave-cometric metric and show no conjugate points via index forms over geodesic passages.
quote: We construct a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a smooth Riemannian metric without conjugate points but admits no smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature.

backbone: Hartogs disc bundle over the ball with Calabi-type potential; construct a base potential defeating holomorphic minorants via mean-preserving measures, and verify complete metric with pinched negative real sectional curvature.
quote: We construct $M$ as a family of discs over the unit ball $\B=\{z\in\C^2:|z|<1\}$.

backbone: Continue the intermediate graph map F_t in t; at a first failing scale, weak MTW plus Jacobi trial fields exclude conjugacy and collisions, giving global support, hence convex injectivity domains.
quote: At a first failing scale, limits from earlier scales show that the relevant finite convex hulls are still minimizing.

backbone: Cone-like metric whose sphere link follows a periodic path of equal-area metrics; eigenline exchanges at double eigenvalues cycle a spectral band, giving many harmonic functions with average rate below k.
quote: We construct a periodic path $H(s)$ of sphere metrics near the round metric, all with the same pointwise area form.

backbone: Bootstrap a signed momentum-increment estimate along characteristics; it lower-bounds each dyadic doubling time of maximal momentum, these sum divergently, so momentum stays bounded and Glassey–Strauss continuation applies.
quote: These lower bounds have a divergent sum, which rules out unbounded momentum support in finite time and allows the continuation criterion to apply.

backbone: Construct a datum with cold annular jets and colored finite evolutions; compactness limits give global conservative entropy solutions, and a cap dilation limit separates two distinct solutions from it.
quote: We construct one nonnegative initial density with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy that gives rise to two distinct such solutions.

backbone: Layered exact finite expansion of interacting histories over time cells, centered against the Boltzmann solution; history integrals and tree counting with a single energy budget bound remainders, summed to convergence.
quote: Their layered expansion retains the earlier histories of correlated remainders while extracting the factors approximated by the kinetic solution.

backbone: Boundary jets and an exterior cap give equal Green matrices; source solutions define a maximal local isometry with bundle map; any interior frontier point is crossed by extension estimates, contradiction.
quote: They define a maximal local isometry with a unitary bundle identification; Section~\ref{sec:boundary} prepares coordinates and harmonic frames at any putative frontier point.

backbone: Reduce to rectifiable minimizers; blow-ups are global generalized minimizers whose classification leaves only bounded compact crack pieces; exclude these by energy comparison, then cited regularity gives the local forms.
quote: In the generalized-limit formulation recalled below, these classification results leave the possible bounded components of a limiting crack as the remaining obstruction.

backbone: Suppose a nonflat homogeneous minimizer in dimension at most six; reduce to a smooth link, build test and vector field via a certified tensor inequality, contradicting stability.
quote: The extra positive mass $\epsilon_*w^{2a}$ will give the contradiction.

backbone: Explicitly build approximating diffeomorphisms: PL approximation on fine meshes with local topological modifications and squeezes controlling W^{1,p} budgets, then strong smoothing of locally finite PL homeomorphisms.
quote: We give the selection, the maps, and the estimates in their order of use.

backbone: Suppose an interior critical point; a vector variational principle, boundary multiplier identity and positive-definite reciprocal-Green kernels force the energy sum to vanish, contradicting nonzero eigenfunction gradient.
quote: Take an arbitrary $0\ne u\in\V$, with $g$ defined by \eqref{eq:g}. Suppose $\Phi(p)$ is a critical point.

backbone: Assume a positive entire solution; Newton-potential bounds, a localized virial identity and an interval-pair pressure inequality yield an energy bound incompatible with scaling in the subcritical range.
quote: The energy bound and the scaling contradiction

backbone: Construct a self-similar profile by inner/exterior matching with a certified Brouwer-degree argument, prove outgoing spectral stability, transfer to the torus, and close nonlinear stability on an open set.
quote: We prove the profile, spectral stability, periodic localization, and openness needed here directly; the cited blowup constructions provide historical and methodological context, not inputs to those proofs.

backbone: Boundary determination and gluing transfer solutions across the boundary; Carleman-estimated physical solutions with transport frames are compared, and a finite-type uniqueness lemma on the null conic recovers both moduli.
quote: The proof converts equality of the boundary maps into an exact exterior comparison of physical solutions.

backbone: Explicit density on five balls with two Coulomb branch families certified by a supporting potential; optimal plans use both branches, and mass imbalance blocks deterministic Monge selection.
quote: We construct a smooth compactly supported probability density on ℝ3, with a smooth compactly supported square root, for which the three-marginal Coulomb transport minimum is not attained by any pair of measure-preserving Borel maps.

backbone: Reduce to finite atomic targets; move Laguerre-cell sites along an optimal coupling, bound cell-moment variation by mass variation, integrate to the one-third bound; three-atom example gives sharpness.
quote: \Cref{sec:cells} establishes the cell calculus and shows that the intercepts realizing prescribed positive masses depend differentiably on the sites.

backbone: Monotone solutions in R^8 reduce via stable end profiles and minimizing cones to stable rigidity in R^7, proved by finite-density rigidity plus an unbounded-density contradiction with a radial ambient test.
quote: Part I gives the complete deduction from stable end profiles to Theorem~\ref{thm:monotone}, conditional on Theorem~\ref{thm:stable}.

backbone: Compile a Turing machine into a reversible recorder whose instructions are reciprocal affine rectangle maps, realize each by seven solenoidal shear stages, and verify the particle tracks the computation.
quote: We realize finite reciprocal affine instruction maps by smooth incompressible shear flows on a flat three-torus.

backbone: If no uniform power rate holds, compactness gives an entire nonaffine limiting solution; an extremal horizontal Jensen defect, barycentric envelopes and propagation force it to be affine, contradiction.
quote: First we reduce failure of a uniform power rate for affine approximation to an entire nonaffine solution of a limiting equation.
